transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
I'm here because I've been losing a lot of weight recently. I've only been eating very small amounts of food each day, and my weight has just kept dropping.
Do you feel very afraid of gaining weight, or do you strongly worry about your body shape or size?

Yes, I am absolutely terrified of gaining even a single pound; the thought of it panics me. When I look in the mirror, I still see myself as way too big, and I just can't shake the constant worry about my body shape.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Anorexia Nervosa, Major Depressive Disorder, Generalized Anxiety Disorder, Adjustment Disorder], but the patient now clearly reports intense fear of gaining weight, persistent body image distortion, and marked restriction of intake with weight loss. This strongly supports Anorexia Nervosa and makes Major Depressive Disorder, Generalized Anxiety Disorder, and Adjustment Disorder less likely because the core symptoms are better explained by an eating disorder rather than a primary mood, anxiety, or stress-related disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports significant weight loss from markedly restricted food intake and an intense fear of gaining weight, with persistent body image distortion/overvaluation of size. These are core features of anorexia nervosa. No evidence of recurrent binge eating or compensatory purging to support bulimia nervosa, and no binge episodes to suggest binge-eating disorder.
